item.title: Communications Officer (AI Specialist) – COMSI – (Contractual)
item.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. The Communications Department (COM) develops and coordinates the IMF’s external and internal communications strategy, shapes key messages, and responds to the evolving global communications environment. The Strategy and Impact Division (COMSI) plays a central role in shaping strategic communication priorities, developing narratives and executive communications, assessing impact, and advancing practical innovation in AI analytics. COMSI is seeking a highly motivated early-career professional to serve as a specialist on AI for communications, enabling the adoption of AI across COM. The successful candidate will help translate AI capabilities into practical approaches for communications work, contribute to piloting and scaling AI tools, and strengthen efforts to embed AI into core workflows in the division and the department, working closely with COM’s AI group. The role combines hands-on experimentation, analytical work, and strategic input, with a strong focus on improving productivity, insight, and communication effectiveness. Duties and Responsibilities Under the supervision of division management and in coordination with the COM AI group, the selected candidate will: Enable practical AI adoption Work with COM teams to identify workflows where AI can improve effectiveness, consistency, or speed. Develop reusable workflows, agents and AI-powered solutions to integrate AI into daily work. Evaluate AI tools, licenses, and workflows to assess usage and cost-effectiveness. Deliver practical training, demonstrations, peer learning, and guidance for COM staff. Promote responsible AI use. Strengthen measurement and insight Assess the impact of AI on productivity and communications outcomes. Conduct AI-assisted analysis of data, including media, social, web, content, and audience signals. Monitor how IMF content is selected, summarized and attributed in AI-enabled search environments. Identify risks and opportunities for IMF content visibility, accuracy, and usability. Strengthen overall impact measurement and analysis work Contribute to strategic communications Turn findings of data analyses into actionable recommendations for decision making by COM teams and management. Create compelling reports and presentations to communicate data-based findings to staff in COM and other departments. Actively participate in research projects on communications Qualifications Educational development, typically acquired by the completion of an advanced university degree, or equivalent, in Communications, Computer Science, International Relations or a related field; or a university degree, or equivalent, supplemented by a minimum of six (6) years of relevant professional experience; or a minimum of two (2) years of relevant experience at grade A08, or equivalent, is required. Competencies Extensive hands-on experience using AI tools, including advanced knowledge of generative AI, agents, plugins, or knowledge-retrieval tools. Strong analytical skills in interpreting data from media, social media, web analytics, dashboards, or audience research, and generating actionable insights for strategic decision making. Familiarity with common corporate business processes and workflows, and the potential of AI solutions to improve them. Strong curiosity about communications and willingness to experiment with new tools and approaches to improve communications outcomes. Sound judgment, including awareness of reputational and ethical considerations in AI use. Flexibility and ability to work collaboratively across teams in a fast-evolving environment. Academic background or work experience in communications, political science or economics, is a plus. This is a one-year contractual appointment. Contractual appointments at the IMF are renewable for up to four years of cumulative contractual service, pending incumbent's performance, budget availability, and continuous business need. item.title: Resident Advisor on Monetary and Foreign Exchange Market Operations (CAPTAC-DR) (MCMTA)
item.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. The Monetary and Capital Markets (MCM) Department of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is seeking a well-qualified professional to work as a resident advisor in monetary and foreign exchange market operations at the IMF Central America, Panama, and the Dominican Republic Regional Technical Assistance Center (CAPTAC-DR). This is a long-term expert (contractual) assignment based in Guatemala City, Guatemala, with a twelve‑month initial term, with a possibility of extension typically up to three to five years based on performance and funding availability. CAPTAC-DR is a multi-donor-financed regional capacity development center, providing capacity development (CD)—technical assistance (TA) and training—to seven jurisdictions in the region, namely Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama and the Dominican Republic. The resident advisor will deliver CD in various aspects of central bank governance, monetary policy implementation, foreign exchange (FX) operations, and central bank liquidity backstops. The advisor will be part of the CAPTAC-DR team ( www.captac-dr.org ) and will be backstopped by the IMF’s MCM Department. Duties and responsibilities The resident advisor will help identify CD needs and respond to requests received by CAPTAC-DR. The resident advisor is expected to travel or provide CD remotely as well as to lead/organize selected training for CAPTAC-DR member countries. By elaborating a well-prioritized medium-term work program, s/he will support CAPTAC-DR member countries through: · Managing and delivering CD on governance, accounting, and central bank financial reporting, central bank communication and transparency, monetary policy implementation and domestic market operations, FX policy implementation, FX reserve management, and FX market development, and central bank liquidity backstops for financial stability, directly and through short-term experts backstopped by the resident advisor. · Managing and delivering CD on monetary modeling and policy analysis, inflation targeting and FX regimes, directly and through short-term experts backstopped by the resident advisor. · Preparing required documents prior to and after each mission for MCM internal review and approval, and ensuring transmission of final documents to the relevant country authorities. · Assessing monetary policy frameworks and advising on central bank operations in line with monetary policy regimes and the central bank mandates. · Organizing, conducting, or facilitating country or regional workshops and seminars/webinars, on monetary and foreign exchange market operations, including collaborating with other resident advisors in CAPTAC-DR. · Liaising, as needed, with other CD providers to ensure complementarity and coordination in the support provided to member countries. · Coordinating with MCM, including backstoppers, on policy areas and keeping them up to date on major developments, to ensure that any advice provided by the advisor is consistent with IMF policies. · Observing the policies and procedures of the IMF, applying the results-based management (RBM) strategic framework in guiding the CD activities undertaken [1]. · Leading annual work planning and budgeting for the CD program in CAPTAC-DR on monetary and FX market operations and contributing to outreach activities and reports on the Center’s activities. Qualifications The successful candidate should demonstrate initiative, strong analytical and sound policy judgment, including the ability to develop innovative solutions to complex policy challenges, and have: · At least five years of relevant experience working in monetary policy and central banking, including experience in one or more of the following areas: monetary policy frameworks and implementation, monetary and FX market operations, reserve management, and monetary modeling and policy analysis. Experience may have been acquired in a central bank, an international organization, or at another relevant national or international institution. · Expertise in technical assistance delivery in this field is an advantage. · A graduate degree in economics, finance, accounting, or a related area. · Excellent interpersonal skills, including the ability: to work and coordinate effectively with stakeholders and senior policymakers in the region and the donor community, to lead and manage teams of senior experts, to work as part of a team that would include staff at IMF headquarters as well as in CAPTAC-DR, to deliver high-quality outputs within agreed timelines, and to handle sensitive and confidential issues with discretion in a multicultural environment. · Strong verbal and written communication skills in English and Spanish, including presentational skills in support of training-related activities. · Good organizational and time management skills in balancing demands from member countries with duties and responsibilities from MCM and CAPTAC-DR. · Proficiency in modern computer systems and applications, including AI. The successful candidate will be selected based on a written test and a panel interview. Compensation and benefits are competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience. [1] The RBM framework focuses on performance and achievement of results, supported by the Fund’s Capacity Development Management and Administration Program (CDMAP). item.title: 2027 Fund Internship Program (FIP) - Economists
item.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. Work on real research. In one summer. The Fund Internship Program (FIP) offers PhD students in economics an outstanding opportunity to contribute to the work of one of the world's leading international financial institutions. As a Fund intern, you'll apply your economic research skills to real-world policy questions that matter to the IMF's 191 member countries. You'll work alongside experienced IMF economists, gain hands-on research experience, strengthen your analytical skills, and build a professional network in a uniquely international environment. Many interns present their findings to IMF staff, and some see their work published internally. If you're passionate about macroeconomics, international policy, and research that can make a global impact, the Fund Internship Program could be your next step. About the Program Over 10 to 12 weeks, you'll contribute to an individual research or project assignment while working alongside experienced IMF staff at IMF Headquarters in Washington, D.C. The internship provides practical experience, exposure to the IMF's work, and the opportunity to apply your academic knowledge to real-world policy and operational challenges. To learn more about the Fund Internship Program and hear from previous interns, visit the Fund Internship Program page on IMF Careers. Eligibility To be considered for the 2027 Fund Internship Program - Economists, you must: Be within one to two years of completing a PhD in macroeconomics or a related field. Be enrolled as a student at the time of the internship and return to your academic studies afterward. Be under the age of 32 when the internship begins in June 2027. Demonstrate excellent written and spoken English. Possess strong analytical, quantitative, and computer skills. Application Requirements As part of your online application, you must complete the technical questionnaire and upload the following documents: Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume Statement of Interest or Cover Letter explaining your motivation for applying to the IMF Evidence of current student status and academic performance , including either: A recent transcript from your current university program, or A letter from your university confirming active enrollment and recent grades. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Only candidates selected for further consideration will be contacted by a member of the FIP recruitment team. Previous participants in the Fund Internship Program are not eligible and should not reapply. Frequently Asked Questions Is the internship paid? Yes. The Fund Internship Program is a full-time, paid internship requiring 40 hours of work per week. How long is the internship? Internships last between 10 and 12 weeks. When do internships begin? The start of 2027 internship is June 7, 2027 (ending August 27, 2027). What visa support does the IMF provide? If you are not a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or otherwise authorized to work in the United States, you will require a G4 visa. The IMF will provide the documentation needed to support your visa application with U.S. authorities. Does the IMF provide housing? No. Interns are responsible for arranging and securing their own housing accommodation. Resources and guidance may be shared with selected interns during the onboarding process. Will I be notified when my application is received? Yes. You will receive an automated confirmation after submitting your application. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further consideration. Are there exceptions to the age limit? The only exception is for time spent in mandatory military service.
